messages:
emma.docs: Heads-up on docs PR #2799: the API reference shows the tracing/request-id header as `Request-Id` (capital I) and marked as required. Runtime actually accepts `X-Request-Id` or `request-id` (case-insensitive) and the header is optional. This is causing curl/examples to fail for some users.

emma.docs: Example in the PR (from generated templates):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \\
  -H 'Request-Id: 1234' \\
  -d '{"model":"xlarge-gen","prompt":"hi"}'
```
Some proxies rewrite/remove `Request-Id` header which made example tests flaky.

dmitri-api: Thanks. We intentionally accept both `X-Request-Id` and `Request-Id` and we normalize to lower-case `request-id` in the request context. Header is optional; when missing we synthesize a server-side id. OpenAPI currently has conflicting entries: one schema fragment marked header required, and the examples show only the capitalized variant. That's our fault.

dmitri-api: Behavior detail: we treat headers case-insensitively (RFC) and accept either header name. We should update the docs to reflect optionality and recommend `X-Request-ID` (common practice).

olivia-sdk: Repro: Go/Java SDK integration tests use the exact header name from docs when asserting request tracing and fail if proxies rewrite it. Also some generated code annotated the header as required which fails compile-time checks in strict API clients.
\em ma.docs: Small but important: we need to change the OpenAPI header object to not set required=true, change examples to include both `X-Request-ID` and show omission case, and add a troubleshooting note: "If you rely on a request id for correlating traces, include X-Request-ID; otherwise the server returns `x-request-id` in response headers."

ci-bot: CI: docs PR #2799 integration tests failing: header/RequestIdHeaderConsistency (see https://ci.internal/rdw/2799/job/21).

sam-security: Quick security note: if we recommend an ID generation pattern, don't expose any internal structure. Use opaque UIDs. Also ensure we don't recommend sending internal user IDs as request ids.

dmitri-api: Good call. We'll state: "use a short opaque UUIDv4 or 128-bit hex token; avoid embedding PII."

olivia-sdk: Plan for SDKs: make header optional in generated clients; add helper that sets `X-Request-ID` automatically when nil (UUID generator). For Go, I'll change the generated struct tag to `header:\"x-request-id,omitempty\"` and add a small example: `req.WithHeader(\"X-Request-ID\", uuid.New().String())`. ETA: 4h.

emma.docs: I'll update three examples: curl (with and without header), JS fetch example showing automatic header helper, and a note in the API reference header table clarifying optionality and normalization. I'll also add a small troubleshooting section: "missing request-id in responses? Check proxies and ensure header isn't filtered" with a link to common proxy configs.

dmitri-api: I'll patch the OpenAPI: remove required flag, add description recommending `X-Request-ID`, and add two canonical examples: one that includes header and one minimal. I'll also add a server response example showing `x-request-id` in response headers.

ci-bot: Reminder: after changes, run the header smoke tests and integration suite.

olivia-sdk: Also note for reviewers: don't break consumers that relied on the header being required. I'll add a compatibility note and bump the major version in the generated clients if needed.

emma.docs: Final checklist: 1) @dmitri-api update OpenAPI and regenerate examples 2) @olivia-sdk open SDK PR to make header optional + helper 3) @emma.docs update API ref + curl/js/py snippets + troubleshooting note 4) @sam-security quick review of wording around token recommendations. Target: EOD today.

dmitri-api: Roger. I'll push an OpenAPI commit now and tag SDK/docs PRs in the description.

ci-bot: CI: OpenAPI commit pushed; waiting on SDK/docs PRs for full pass.
